For a curious ten-year-old, **Python** is almost always the best starting point. Here’s why:  - **Readable**: It looks like pseudocode. You can write `print("Hello, world!")` and it works — no weird symbols or strict syntax rules that trip you up early. - **Huge library of tools**: From drawing pictures with text (`turtle`) to scraping websites, playing music, or even making simple games, Python has something for almost any hobby a kid might have. - **Great community & help**: If they get stuck (and they will), there are tutorials, forums, and even kids’ coding clubs that use it as their go-to language.  A few other options worth mentioning: - **Scratch** (visual blocks): Great for absolute beginners who want to see instant results without typing — but it’s more of a stepping stone than a real programming language. - **JavaScript**: Good if they’re interested in web stuff, but its syntax is messier and can be frustrating when things break.  If I had to pick one: Python. It balances ease of use with enough power to grow into something serious later.

scores.answerPreview: A hash map (or hash table) is a data structure that stores key-value pairs using a hash function to compute an index for direct access, enabling fast lookups and insertions in constant average time. It works by taking keys, applying them through a hash function that returns an integer bucket number, then storing values at those locations so you can retrieve them instantly when you need the corresponding value.
